Ana (Product): follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A on pricing/packaging. captured a couple customer questions here to convert into a short FAQ: 1) how do rate limits work across Hosted vs Dedicated (reserved capacity + burst credits)? 2) when are credits consumed if there are retries or backoffs?

Leo (CEO): tl;dr - rate limiting is independent from billing. Hosted customers have a short burst buffer that draws from credits; Dedicated customers get reserved throughput and may have negotiated burst rules. Credits/tokens are billed at emission time (when the model actually outputs tokens), not at request enqueue.

Sandeep (Eng): detailed enforcement model: layered approach - per-key ingress TokenBucket, model-level emission accounting, and cluster admission for Dedicated pools. snippet: 

```yaml
ingress_policy:
  rpm: 3600
  burst: 200
emission_billing:
  tokens_per_minute: 1200000
  billing_point: "on_emit"
```

Jess (Engineering): Hosted behavior: temporary burst window (~5 minutes) where extra RPS is served from a burst bucket (consumes credits). Once the burst bucket is exhausted requests either queue briefly or return 429 depending on route SLOs. Dedicated: reserved GPUs serve regular traffic; short bursts may be covered by idle reserved capacity (no credit consumption) up to contract burst_factor. Beyond that, system throttles or routes to fallback models.

Mike (Finance): clarifying question - for enterprise accounts with committed spend, do we auto-bill overages?

Leo (CEO): Hosted customers auto-consume prepay credits or are invoiced based on plan. For Dedicated enterprise customers, overages are billed at negotiated rates; large overages trigger alerts and require account approval unless customer opted into auto-billing.

Lisa (Support): can we get a paste-ready FAQ blurb? customers are confused about 429 vs being charged.

Ana (Product): suggested FAQ blurb: "If you hit your plan's rate limit you may receive a 429. Tokens are charged only when the model emits tokens. Hosted customers have a short burst buffer which may consume credits; Dedicated customers often cover small bursts with reserved capacity. If unsure, provide your org id and support will check your burst and credit state."

Jess (Engineering): operational note - retries can increase token consumption if the retry reaches the model and it emits before the client cancels. recommend idempotency keys for non-streaming calls and client-side early cancel on duplicates.

Sandeep (Eng): i'll open a docs PR with exact defaults (burst window, default RPS, 429 vs queue behavior) and an internal SE runbook. will post the PR link here.

Ana (Product): action items: 1) @Sandeep create docs PR + FAQ, 2) @Jess add runtime comment about billing_point, 3) @Mike confirm enterprise overage flow, 4) @Lisa add FAQ to Zendesk. tagging ops for sign-off. :thumbsup:

DocsBot: PR created -> https://git.redwood.internal/docs/pull/4078 (proposed FAQ + config examples).

Ana (Product): leaving thread open for any edge cases. paste customer-facing wording here before publish.
